The changes improve both solution quality and practical runtime:

- **Exact optimization expands from 10 to 12 destinations**, allowing hidden configurations with 11–12 receivers to receive a true minimum-cost shared broadcast tree rather than a greedy approximation.
- **Costless/undefined-cost edges are excluded**, preventing NetworkX from silently treating missing monetary costs as default edge weights.
- **Graph pruning removes irrelevant relays**, reducing subset-DP state work while preserving every node that can lie on a source-to-destination route.
- **The large-destination fallback now evaluates multiple seeded trees**, avoiding the strong dependence of greedy shared-tree construction on which destination is attached first. This can find lower-cost common prefixes and relay branches without the exponential cost of full Steiner DP.
- The topology output format remains unchanged: every destination partition receives the path induced by the selected shared broadcast tree.
